newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rexrodt sees further steps to Telekom sale this yr.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt sees further steps to Telekom sale this yr.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Monday he could imagine Bonn taking further steps towards privatising Deutsche Telekom this year.
Speaking on the sidelines of OECD ministerial talks in Paris, he did not give any further details of a possible further sale of shares drawn from Bonn's remaining 74 percent stake.
"I could imagine that we agree further steps towards privatising Deutsche Telekom this year to a strategic investor," Rexrodt told a news conference.
The government floated 26 percent of Deutsche Telekom last November in an issue which raised 20 billion marks ($11.9 billion).

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said earlier this month Bonn was considering an early sale of additional shares in Telekom later this year but said it would not help Germany meet deficit target criteria for entry into the single currency.

Instead, Waigel said the proceeds of his plan, which has drawn criticism since Bonn is obliged under law not to sell any more shares on stock exchanges before the year 2000, would be used to pay off old debt.
Bonn has not said what portion of its 74 percent stake of Telekom's 2.7 billion shares, which is valued at about 80 billion marks at current market prices, would be sold.
